message.content:
Here’s a quick‑reference guide to keep your piano sounding its best:

| # | Tip | Why it matters |
|---|-----|----------------|
| **1** | Keep the room at stable temperature (65–75 °F / 18–24 °C) and relative humidity around 45–55%. | Wood expands/contracts with moisture changes – this keeps action parts from sticking or cracking. |
| **2** | Use a hygrometer & humidifier/dehumidifier as needed. | Prevents “dry” conditions that cause strings to stretch too tight or wood to warp. |
| **3** | Cover the piano when not playing. | Protects against dust, light damage, and sudden temperature swings. |
| **4** | Clean regularly but gently. | Wipe down keys, lid, and outer surfaces with a soft microfiber cloth. Avoid harsh chemicals—use a mild soap solution if necessary. |
| **5** | Dust inside only during scheduled service. | Accumulated dust on hammers and soundboard can affect tone; professional technicians know how to do it safely. |
| **6** | Tune at least twice a year (or more often if you play frequently). | Piano strings change tension over time; regular tuning maintains pitch accuracy. |
| **7** | Check the pedal operation monthly. | Ensure pedals move freely without binding; replace worn pads promptly. |
| **8** | Inspect the action mechanism quarterly. | Look for loose key pins, sticky felt, or misaligned components. A technician can adjust or replace them before they become major issues. |
| **9** | Move the piano slowly and carefully. | Pianos are heavy and delicate; moving them improperly can crack frames or shift internal parts. |
| **10** | Store music sheets properly. | Avoid placing heavy books directly on top of the piano—they can press into the frame and distort the soundbox. |
| **11** | Maintain the interior hardware. | Tighten screws and bolts periodically; loosened fasteners can lead to uneven vibrations. |
| **12** | Schedule an annual comprehensive inspection. | A qualified tech will check everything—from strings and bridges to the soundboard—and perform preventive repairs. |

### Quick Checklist for Daily Care
- [ ] Close the lid after each session to reduce exposure to air currents.
- [ ] Lightly wipe the keys with a dry cloth to remove fingerprints.
- [ ] Verify that no foreign objects have fallen under the keyboard.
- [ ] Make sure the piano sits level on a firm surface.

By following these habits, you'll preserve both the mechanical integrity and tonal beauty of your piano for years to come!
